issues.title: Comparison with rfc6754
issues.author: fenner
issues.body: Since rfc6754 is about ECMP, we should have a comparison/justification in this document

comments.author: arista-skumar
comments.body:
Comparison:

| Aspect | RFC 6754: ECMP Redirect | Deterministic-ECMP draft |
|---|---|---|
| Core model | Reactive, upstream-directed correction | Proactive, independently reproducible selection |
| Operation | Upstream router tells a downstream router where to redirect PIM Joins | Each downstream router selects from eligible RPF neighbors itself |
| Coordination | Explicit PIM ECMP Redirect message | Common deterministic hash; no per-flow redirect signaling |
| Initial behavior | Downstream selects an RPF path normally, then may be redirected | Downstream hashes before it transmits the Join |
| Scope/topology | Parallel, single-hop ECMP links in a configured ECMP bundle | Two-tier Router-ID selection plus Color for arbitrary multi-tier networks |
| Selection policy | Administratively selected preference and metric; lower numeric values win | Bob Jenkins one-at-a-time hash; highest hash value wins |
| Control traffic | Rate-limited redirects, only when a correction is needed | PIM Hello information; no corrective per-`(S,G)` message |

```text
RFC 6754
--------
Downstream makes an initial ECMP choice
  -> Upstream detects duplicate or non-preferred forwarding
  -> Upstream sends an ECMP Redirect
  -> Downstream joins the requested neighbor/interface and prunes its old path

This draft
-------------------------
Routers determine the same eligible neighbors
  -> Each calculates a specified hash using (S, G, Router-ID or Color)
  -> Each selects the same highest-ranked candidate
  -> Joins converge on that candidate without a redirect

RFC 6754 and the draft solve adjacent but distinct problems. 

- Choose **RFC 6754's model** when an upstream router must dynamically impose
  an administrative preference and can correct already-created PIM state.
- Choose **The draft model** when the primary requirement is
  for independently operating routers to select the same upstream neighbor from
  the beginning, especially in a Clos or other multi-tier data-center fabric.
- Combined model is also possible.
```

issues.title: How to evaluate hash function quality
issues.author: fenner
issues.body: In the meeting room at IETF122, there were some questions about how to evaluate the choice of a hash function. Is the Jenkins hash the right one? Can we compare it with the hash in the PIM spec (widely known to be poor quality, and the IPv6 handling is even worse, but - rather than saying "xor is bad", let's say "we evaluate by this metric")
